title: Auto Loans: Interest Owed at Payoff
content:
When a borrower clears an Auto Loans account using a transfer out of PCB checking, the sum includes interest right up to the credit date. This note defines that interest.

## Definition

The interest is the capital balance multiplied by the annual percentage rate, divided by one hundred and again by the product's day count, and multiplied by the count of calendar dates in the span that opens the day after the last payment date and closes on the credit date, inclusive of the credit date. For a same-day payoff the credit date is today. Rounding happens a single time, half-up to the cent,, on the finished figure.

## Counting the span (hypothetical dates)

| Last payment date | Credit date | Calendar dates counted |
|---|---|---|
| 28 February 2031 | 10 March 2031 | 10 (1 to 10 March) |
| 10 March 2031 | 10 March 2031 | 0 |
| 31 December 2030 | 2 January 2031 | 2 |

## Rounding point (invented figures)

If the unrounded interest for the span came to 57.3350, the payoff carries 57.34; the rounding is done only on that final figure.
